profile.address: 717 South Wells Street, Suite 600, Chicago, IL 60607
profile.reading: Netrality's Chicago data center occupies 717 South Wells Street, Suite 600, in the city's Financial District, Chicago, Illinois 60607. Netrality's own facility page describes 100,000 square feet of colocation space, 12,400 kilovolt diverse utility feeds, N+1 backup generator power with a 5,700 gallon fuel supply, N+1 UPS redundancy, and 600 tons of 2N chilled water cooling delivered through Kyoto and Delta Cube cooling units. A third party aggregator, DataCenterMap, independently lists this building's power capacity as 5 megawatts, with a stated power density of 125 watts per square foot for critical systems capacity, a 1.5 megawatt diesel generator, and 500 to 600 kilowatt UPS systems distributed across multiple floors. Netrality's own page lists SSAE 16 SOC 2 Type 2, HIPAA, and PCI compliance, and states the facility hosts more than 29 on net network providers including AT&T, Verizon, Lumen, Cogent, and Zayo, along with 19 peering networks, 2 internet exchanges, and cloud connections to Lumen Cloud Connect, Megaport, and Zayo CloudLink. Netrality Data Centers is a carrier hotel and colocation operator focused on network dense, interconnection oriented buildings in secondary US markets, with other facilities in Kansas City and St. Louis already on file elsewhere in this registry. No specific year built was located for this building this session. Chicago's Financial District, known as "the Loop," has long hosted major carrier hotel buildings given the city's central role in US long haul fiber routes connecting the East and West coasts, a legacy shared with larger carrier hotel buildings elsewhere in the Loop tracked under other operators in this registry, such as 350 East Cermak. Netrality's portfolio strategy focuses on acquiring and operating this kind of legacy telecom or financial district building in secondary and network dense markets, rather than building new hyperscale campuses, positioning the company differently from wholesale operators like Digital Realty or Equinix that are also tracked elsewhere in this registry.

reading.body:
This facility in Chicago publishes no power capacity figure and no IT load specification. Without published megawatts or rack counts, its scale relative to AI infrastructure cannot be assessed from operator disclosures. The facility is ranked seventh among Illinois sites with published capacity, but this ranking reflects only the six other facilities that have disclosed power figures; most of the 44 mapped facilities in the state publish no specifications at all.

Netrality operates as a carrier hotel and colocation provider focused on network density and interconnection rather than large-scale compute capacity. The published sources do not specify whether this Chicago facility hosts GPU clusters, accelerator cards, or training workloads, nor do they disclose power allocation to AI tenants versus other uses.

Illinois has 236 MW of published data center capacity across six disclosed facilities. Without a power figure from this site, it cannot be determined whether this campus contributes meaningfully to that total or represents a smaller colocation venue. The absence of published specifications is itself informative: this facility does not appear to market itself as an AI-scale destination in its public materials.
